coverage.section_1_floors_and_ceilings: depth 0 and 60; epi 0 and 1000; amplitude 0.1 and 1e8; noise 0.01 and 1e7; correction -1.0 and +1.0; 1 to 40 recordings; 50 events and 200 stations in limits.jsonl; code lengths 1-5; id lengths 1-20; channels per station 1-4; contributing counts 0,1,2,3,4 .. 12, 40 (odd and even).

coverage.boundaries: 10 and 600 km exactly are reached in table_ends, gain, correction and limits, only via exact pairs (numeric_discipline in seal.py enforces sqrt==hypot at the ends, or a margin of at least 1e-3 km). Three-times ties are binary-exact only (1.5/0.5, 300/100, 0.75/0.25, 40/20 excluded, 12/0.5) and non-ties sit at least 1e-9 away. CR-1 and CR-5 are closed on the verifier side.
coverage.envelope_phrases: 'a station sitting on the epicentre' (epi 0 in hypocentral and off_table), 'out to 1000 km' (off_table), 'sites whose broadband and strong-motion sensors arrive as separate recordings' (shared_station, including the two-station three-recording null event and a median shift), 'channels of every noise level' (readings), 'positive, zero and negative corrections' (correction), 'one, two, three or many contributing stations, odd and even' (fewer_than_three, three, median, median_even).

semantic_equivalence: The tolerance is 1e-6 on distance_km and ml, as written. id, code, contributes, list lengths and order, and null are exact. Key sets are exact, as 6.2 requires. Numbers must be int or float, not bool; contributes must be a bool. No unstated order is enforced. The expected values are rounded to 1e-10 at sealing, well inside the band.
isolation_harness: Separate verifier image; no-network. The delivered driver bytes are read at module import, before any candidate code runs, and the verifier's copy is then os.replace-d onto the documented path. Candidate code runs via setpriv as uid/gid 65534 with --no-new-privs and cleared groups, env -i, python3 -I -S, in its own session with group kill, from a fresh cwd, on a neutral /tmp/.../bulletin.json. No case label reaches the candidate. /tests and /logs/verifier are chmod 700 before the run, and a test asserts nobody cannot read /tests, the ROSTER, test_outputs.py or /logs/verifier. The driver is byte-checked before and after. Expectations are pinned by sha256 and row count, and every bulletin is re-validated against section 1 on load. One overall deadline of 1500 s is well within timeout_sec 1800; with 22 subprocess runs, the run should take seconds.
solution_correctness: fix.patch matches NPM-4 on every rule. It keeps the shipped log end-segment extrapolation outside 10-600 km, fed with hypocentral distance. It pools a station's amplitudes across its recordings and reports that one value on each of its rows. It counts each station once in the median and the minimum of three. model.py agrees with my independently written reference on every sealed bulletin.

findings.issue: 'Each departure reverted alone and each natural over-repair ... fails only its own test' is inaccurate for the reverted departures. Also consider dropping 'lower middle value' from the over-repair list, or saying it fails median_even among others, since it fails 10 files.

findings.issue: -S disables site-packages for the candidate's package. That is harmless here: the image is stdlib-only and the agent has no network. But it is an unstated constraint, and it would reject a solution that pip-installed a library into the agent image.
findings.suggested_fix: None required. Optionally mention it in verification_explanation, which already says 'python3 -I -S'.
